newsitem.title: USA: States move to subpoena Staples merger records.
newsitem.headline: States move to subpoena Staples merger records.

text.p: Maryland and other states moved to subpoena merger records from Staples Inc. and Office Depot Inc. on Tuesday, after the two office superstore chains refused to turn over the records voluntarily.
The Maryland state attorney general's office announced it had served subpoenas Tuesday, and the states of New York and California said they would serve papers Wednesday.
The Federal Trade Commission is already in U.S. District Court seeking to block the proposed $4 billion merger, contending it would raise prices to consumers.

"We have today served civil investigative demands on Staples and Office Depot," said Ellen Cooper, the Maryland assistant attorney general in charge of the antitrust division. "Our minimum return date is always three working days, and we'd like to get the information as soon as possible."

An official with the New York state attorney general's office said it was about to serve the subpoenas. In California, Kathleen Foote of the attorney general's office said her office expected to serve the subpoenas Wednesday.
The states asked Staples and Office Depot to let them look at the records obtained by the FTC.
But the chains won a ruling in federal court late Monday that kept secret hundreds of boxes of proprietary documents containing price and strategic information.
Under the ruling, the states would be permitted to look at the material only if they became parties to the case and were bound by the outcome.
The states said they needed to review the material before deciding what legal action to take.
An attorney for Staples said the chains had not decided how to respond to the subpoenas.
"We're going to talk about it tonight," said attorney Robert Paul in Washington. "I'm not sure what we're going to do."
He said the range of possibilities extended from fighting in court to withhold any materials from the states to agreeing to turn over all materials they had requested.
